source.title: LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders
source.authors: Zheng Chai; Qin Ren; Xijun Xiao; Huizhi Yang; Bo Han; Sijun Zhang; Di Chen; Hui Lu; Wenlin Zhao; Lele Yu; Xionghang Xie; Shiru Ren; Xiang Sun; Yaocheng Tan; Peng Xu; Yuchao Zheng; Di Wu

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law measurements to supervised industrial recommendation models, rather than reproducing language-model pretraining scaling.
record.gate_note: Included the LONGER scaling sweeps: sequence length versus AUC and LogLoss, and parameter count and FLOPs versus AUC. The paper evaluates supervised CVR prediction, not held-out language-model pretraining loss. Its baseline and ablation comparisons are not scaling-law results and are omitted.
record.test_reason: Fits power laws of offline CVR AUC against parameter count and FLOPs for one transformer recommender (LONGER) on a 5.2B-sample industrial dataset. This is a new setting, with results on whether the power-law form extends beyond text pretraining (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The scaling claims come from the abstract and Section 4.3 ('industrial-level scaling laws'); the Conclusions section itself emphasises efficiency and deployability, not scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures supervised industrial recommendation CVR performance (AUC and LogLoss), using sequence length, parameter count, and FLOPs as scaling factors; it does not reproduce language-model pretraining-loss experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Sequence-length curves are reported separately by depth (1, 2, 4, and 10 layers); the text says deeper models benefit more from longer sequences, with diminishing returns in AUC improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: AUC rises and LogLoss falls with input user-behaviour sequence length (300 to 5k) at depths 1, 2, 4 and 10, with power-law fits of R² 0.95 to 0.99. Gains diminish with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recommendation-model performance scales as a power law in input context (behaviour-sequence) length.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the Nineteenth ACM Conference on Recommender Systems (RecSys '25)
record.problems: The scaling results concern one proposed recommender model and a supervised industrial CVR task, not language-model pretraining. Numerical fits are presented in figures; no uncertainty estimates are stated, and the paper does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 baseline comparisons, Table 2 component/query ablations, and online A/B-test metrics were omitted because they do not report the scaling-law measurements relevant to the tested version.

untested.parts: Other modalities and regimes (image, video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer). Loss rather than AUC versus parameters. Scaling of training data size. Ranges beyond one order of magnitude.
Extrapolation from small to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal allocation of parameters and tokens.
Shape effects at fixed parameter count. Depth is varied only together with parameter count.

record.verdict_notes: The fitted curves show tiny effective ranges (AUC about 0.851 to 0.855). Equations as extracted omit the γ offset, and the LogLoss exponents appear positive, likely a lost minus sign. The ablation and A/B results are correctly left out. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small language-model runs predict much larger runs.
The loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation at fixed compute, and how that allocation varies with compute.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Other modalities and training regimes beyond supervised industrial recommendation; the paper tests only LONGER on its recommendation task.
Downstream task performance in language models as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Whether fitted laws depend on setup or fitting choices in the ways described, whether published laws disagree, and whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: LONGER
rows.size_stated: varied hidden dimension; parameter counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Scaled hidden dimension and measured AUC.
rows.note: The text says AUC rises steadily with parameter count, follows a strong power-law trend, and shows no sign of saturation in the tested range.
rows.check:
Several caveats:
- The metric is AUC, not loss; no LogLoss-vs-params curve is reported.
- Parameters span only about 10^6 to 10^7, one decade.
- The fitted exponent is about 0.001 and the γ offset is not displayed.
- No uncertainty is reported.
- size_stated should note the plotted range of about 1e6 to 1e7 params.

rows.subject: LONGER
rows.operation_detail: Varied layer count and sequence length and measured AUC against FLOPs.

conditions.value: varied; specific sweep values not stated

rows.note: The text says AUC rises steadily with FLOPs and follows a strong power-law trend.
rows.check:
Caveats:
- FLOPs are per-example model FLOPs (about 1e9 to 1e10), varied through depth and sequence length, not a training-compute budget.
- The range is one decade, the metric is AUC, and no uncertainty is reported.

relationships.condition: LONGER CVR recommender, AUC vs parameters (width-scaled, 2 layers, seq 2000) and vs FLOPs (d=32), each over about one decade
relationships.reason: r9 and r10 report power-law fits of AUC with R² 0.987 and 0.967. The support is weak: there is no uncertainty, the range is one decade, the exponent is about 0.001, and the metric is AUC, not loss.
relationships.display_finding: AUC power-law fits achieved R² of 0.987 for parameters and 0.967 for FLOPs, with an exponent around 0.001 over roughly one decade.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
